what: Size and ownership distribution of the accounts a Raydium AMM v4 transaction enumerates, measured live — the premise for the `hydrate --account-data` pass (cap, executable handling, absence rate).
method: recent finalized txs → canonical account list (static ++ loaded writable ++ loaded readonly) → batched getMultipleAccounts, full bytes (no dataSlice) → exact byte length per address; executable flag and owner per address

cap_bytes.why: p95 is 4483 B; only 5 of 428 observed addresses exceed 16384 B (1.2%); the worst observed account is 1,048,588 B, so an uncapped pass would move ~100x more bytes per row than the p50 row needs (115 KB vs 9.8 KB stored under the cap).
cap_bytes.measured_rejected: no cap: per-row stored bytes p50 115,036 (11.7x the capped figure) with a single 1 MB account per few rows

executable_handling.rule: program code is delivered as a flag plus its true size, never as bytes
executable_handling.why: the two largest accounts in run 1 (105,032 B and 74,800 B) are BPFLoader-owned program binaries; journaling them as event data would be wrong in a different way than truncating state is.

absence_rule.rule: an address the chain no longer has is recorded in `missing`, with no data entry
absence_rule.why: 16.8% (40/238) and 18.0% (77/428) of enumerated addresses no longer exist at fetch time.

rpc_semantics_pinned_live.space_under_slice: getMultipleAccounts with dataSlice {offset:0,length:16384} on a 1,048,588 B account reports space=1048588 and delivers 16384 bytes — the real size is available without a second full fetch
rpc_semantics_pinned_live.at_cap_probe: getMultipleAccounts with dataSlice {offset:16384,length:1} returns the account again when more data exists beyond the cap, and null when the account is gone OR ends exactly at the cap — an ambiguity the product reports as truncation_verified=false instead of guessing
rpc_semantics_pinned_live.zero_byte_account: an account with 0 bytes of data still returns an entry (not null); null means the account does not exist

limits: one program window (Raydium AMM v4) on mainnet-beta; the distribution of other programs' accounts is not measured
sizes are measured at fetch time, not at event time
the probe reads full account bytes and is not a cheap operation on a public endpoint
